title: Google Tanks... Most Aren't Ready For What This Means
creator: MarketBeat
summary: MarketBeat host Bridget interviews Altimetry Research's Rob Spivey and Joel Litman on Alphabet's 12% post-earnings drop (about $400B of market cap) and whether it signals a crack in the AI bubble. Their answer is no: search still grew around 15% and YouTube about 10% — the misses were roughly $1.5B on search and $200M on YouTube ads — while Google Cloud beat by $1.6B with 100% year-over-year growth, and they argue the earnings miss is exaggerated by accounting that punishes innovation (SpaceX mark-to-market losses, R&D expensed rather than capitalised) plus investment-led negative free cash flow. They call the weakness a buying opportunity for Google at about 17x earnings. They then give three buys and two avoids: Microsoft (a 'best long idea' on Azure and its own chips), Generac (GNRC — commercial standby power gaining pricing power as Caterpillar sits 3-4 years backlogged; uniform ROI 16% versus 3% reported), and AMD (true returns far above the reported 3-4%, winning both GPU share and an unpriced CPU inference leg); and avoids on CoreWeave (CRWV) and Cipher Digital (CIFR), both neoclouds squeezed without pricing power, with Cipher forecast at a negative 20% return on assets in 2026. The episode also promotes their 'Elon Shadow Trust' dividend report. Calls made: GOOGL — BUY, MSFT — BUY, GNRC — BUY, AMD — BUY (all new or reiterated with no stance flip), CRWV — AVOID, CIFR — AVOID. No stated price levels. Caption garbles: 'Generac' rendered as 'Generrack', 'CoreWeave' as 'Cororeweave', 'Cipher' as 'Cippher'.

calls.video_title: Google Tanks... Most Aren't Ready For What This Means
calls.price_at_call: No price level given; after a 12% drop
calls.thesis: Guests Rob Spivey and Joel Litman (Altimetry Research): the drop is an emotional reaction, not a crack in the AI story — search still grew ~15%, YouTube ~10%, and Cloud beat by $1.6B with 100% growth; 'a good buying day for Google' at ~17x PE.
calls.bull_case: Cloud doubling with a $513B to $560B backlog being consumed as revenue; accounting (SpaceX mark-to-market, R&D expensing) exaggerates the earnings miss.
calls.bear_case: Search missed by ~$1.5B and YouTube ads by ~$200M; negative free cash flow as investment ramps.

calls.video_title: Google Tanks... Most Aren't Ready For What This Means
calls.thesis: Guests' 'best long idea': Azure plus Microsoft-designed chips put it in the right parts of the AI value chain; the market is not pricing coming earnings growth or an AI-driven ROA lift.
calls.bull_case: Azure capacity expansion keeps producing revenue beats (cloud revenue $63B, +30% YoY); headcount leverage raises revenue per employee.
calls.bear_case: Copilot adoption softer than hoped, though guests say it does not need to carry the thesis given Azure.

calls.video_title: Google Tanks... Most Aren't Ready For What This Means
calls.thesis: Generac's commercial standby-power business is now structurally more profitable with pricing power: Caterpillar is 3-4 years backlogged, Generac has capacity and just completed a major commercial expansion; uniform ROI was 16% last year (vs 3% reported), forecast 20%+.
calls.bull_case: Behind-the-meter power demand from hyperscalers bypasses political friction over data-centre buildout; residential monopoly (70-80% share) intact.
calls.bear_case: Stock has drifted down since June/July on the narrative that the AI infrastructure boom is over.

calls.video_title: Google Tanks... Most Aren't Ready For What This Means
calls.thesis: Same uniform-accounting case as their 2015 $2 call: true return on assets is multiples of the reported 3-4%; AMD fills hyperscaler demand that does not need top Nvidia chips, and is the only chipmaker on both the GPU and CPU sides.
calls.bull_case: Taking share from Nvidia plus an unpriced second leg as inference shifts toward CPUs, where AMD's GPU-CPU integration wins.
calls.bear_case: Multi-year Nvidia contracts could limit room; guests dismiss this — demand growth leaves room for everyone.

calls.video_title: Google Tanks... Most Aren't Ready For What This Means
calls.price_at_call: No price level given; reiterated after steep falls
calls.thesis: CoreWeave sits in the worst part of the value chain: squeezed by chip suppliers above and plenty of alternative capacity below, with no frontier model of its own; uniform ROA of 2-3% is genuinely correct, economic profit negative and forecast to stay negative — 'get out' and 'still stay out'.
calls.bull_case: The company may survive by eking out just enough to cover debt costs — but survival is not a reason to own it.
calls.bear_case: 'The WeWork of this space'; further to fall than to recover; neocloud hype unwinding.

calls.video_title: Google Tanks... Most Aren't Ready For What This Means
calls.thesis: Cipher Digital (ex Cipher Mining, a Bitcoin miner rebranded as a neocloud) sells a commodity — a 'dumb box' — with no pricing power; forecast at a negative 20% return on assets in 2026.
calls.bull_case: Only neoclouds with huge scale plus power already in place could earn a superior return short-term; Cipher is not one.
calls.bear_case: Same squeeze as CoreWeave: hyperscalers hold the genuine assets and software; rebranding as AI-exposed does not create a moat.
